name: Kusu
confidence_why: Known only second-hand, as quoted in another work.
catalog_citation: Labaere, Hubert R. 2001. Guthrie et la Zone C. Traduction et commentaire du point de vue ɔtɛtɛla C71. Annales Aequatoria 22: 163-183 (French translation, with commentary, of Guthrie, Malcolm. 1948. The Classification of the Bantu Languages. London: IAI/OUP, pp. 36-39, Zone C characteristics; the stress item is Guthrie's zone-level generalisation, relayed). Identity of Kusu as the eastern Otetela dialect: same article p.164; Jacobs, John. 1962. De belangrijkste elementen van het Tetela-toonsysteem. Africana Linguistica 1: 31-42, p.31; Motingea Mangulu. 1989. Sur les parlers Nkutsu. Annales Aequatoria 10: 269-280, p.278.
catalog_locator: Labaere 2001, p.164 (page numbers are footers) for 'le dialecte kusu', and p.172, section 'I. Caractéristiques communes à la Zone C', items 9-11 (item 10 = stress).
catalog_quote: [p.164] L’aire ttla, la langue parlée par les Ankutshu-Ánáámng (ainsi s’exprimaient les participants au congrès de Lodja en mars 1960) est située à l’extrême sud-est de la zone C, entre le 2° et 5° L S et le 22° et 26° L E. On peut distinguer trois régions: la région médiane dont le parler mnjá/ewango est accepté comme norme ttla; la région droite, entre Lomamé et Lualaba où l’on parle le dialecte kusu; la région gauche, entre 22° et 23° L E où l’on parle le ohendó/indanga ou nkutshu. [...] [p.172] 9. Une seule more (quantité) seulement sur la voyelle de radicaux. (De même dans les Zones A,B,D.) COMMENTAIRE En ttla il y a quelques cas de voyelle longue, mais ce semble être toujours par élision de consonne et assimilation vocalique, exemples naanya détruire/punir; ncuuwála/ncuwuwálá être sans ardeur, ncééta blesser (par une flèche). 10. Accent d'intensité sur la syllabe du radical (Ainsi en Zone B.) 11. Ton lexical tant sur le radical que sur les suffixes. (Ainsi en Zones B,D,L)

new_statements.translation: [p.163] Three regions can be distinguished: the middle region whose Monja/Ewango speech is accepted as the Otetela norm; the right-hand region, between the Lomami and the Lualaba, where the Kusu dialect is spoken; the left-hand region ... where Ohendo/Indanga or Nkutshu is spoken. [p.171] 9. Only one mora (quantity) on radical vowels ... COMMENTARY: In Otetela there are a few cases of long vowels, but this always seems to be through consonant elision and vowel assimilation ... 10. Intensity accent (stress) on the radical syllable (likewise in Zone B). 11. Lexical tone on the radical as well as on the suffixes.
new_statements.citation: Labaere, Hubert R. 2001. Guthrie et la Zone C. Traduction et commentaire du point de vue otetela C71. Annales Aequatoria 22: 163-183 (translating Guthrie, M. 1948. The Classification of the Bantu Languages, pp.36-39).
new_statements.locator: printed p.163 (p.159) for the Kusu identification; printed p.171 (p.167), 'I. Caracteristiques communes a la Zone C', items 9-11
new_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (+, per-page extracted text). Both quoted passages are present with the wording given, differences being only stripped diacritics (intensite/intensité, Lomame/Lomamé, 'otetela' for the text's 'ɔtɛtɛla' whose open vowels dropped out) and the printed page numbers, which are off by one: the article's page numbers are footers, so 'la region droite, entre Lomame et Lualaba ou l'on parle le dialecte kusu' sits on p.159 = printed p.164 (not 163), and Guthrie's Zone C item '10. Accent d'intensité sur la syllabe du radical (Ainsi en Zone B.)' sits on p.167 = printed p.172 (not 171; the tete1250 held by the project also says p.172). I read the whole section 'I. Caractéristiques communes…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Guthrie's Zone C generalisation, reproduced by the Otetela grammarian Labaere without objection for the Tetela group (of which he names Kusu as the eastern dialect): dynamic stress falls on the radical (stem-initial) syllable; the language is otherwise tonal (two level tones, H and L, per Jacobs 1962 for 'Tetela-Kusu').
new_statements.exceptions: None; Labaere adds no Otetela- or Kusu-specific comment to item 10 (he does comment on items 9, 12, 13 and corrects Guthrie on other points).
new_statements.domain_note: Zone-level typological statement (Guthrie 1948, Zone C 'caracteristiques communes'), transmitted second-hand; applied to Otetela C71 with Kusu treated as its eastern dialect region. No Kusu-specific first-hand statement on stress was found in any opened source; Jacobs 1962 (first-hand, 'Tetela-Kusu') describes tone only and is silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Every accessible source treats Kusu (C72, kusu1252) as the eastern, Maniema part of the Tetela continuum (tete1250): Jacobs 1962 p.31 'Het Tetela, ook Kusu genaamd ten oosten van de Lomami' (area incl. Kibombo, SW Kindu, Mweho in Kasongo, Lubunda in Kongolo) but his tone description rests on the Tshumbe/Wembo-Nyama C71 dialects; Motingea 1989: 'le Nkutsu de Kindu est indiscutablement un dialecte tetela' (87.67% cognate); Labaere & Shango 1989 file the Akusu of Lubefu/Kibombo under the Odya dialect; Labaere 2001 calls it 'le dialecte kusu' of Otetela. The quoted stress statement is Guthrie's Zone C generalisation applied to Otetela C71, not a Kusu-specific observation. False friends excluded: Bukusu (Luhya, Kenya; Austen 1974-75 IU thesis printed as 'Bakusu' in AA 14), Yakusu (BMS station, Lokele), Basankusu (Equateur town).

sources.citation: Jacobs, John. 1962. De belangrijkste elementen van het Tetela-toonsysteem (Kasayi-Kivu, Congo). Africana Linguistica 1: 31-42. DOI 10.3406/aflin.1962.856.
sources.note: Tone description only. p.31 defines the object as Tetela 'ook Kusu genaamd ten oosten van de Lomami', area explicitly including gewest Kibombo and SW Kindu (the Kusu area), but the description is based on the Tshumbe/Wembo-Nyama (C71) dialects. p.32: 'Het Tetela beschikt over twee tonemen: een gelijkmatig hoog en een gelijkmatig laag toneem'; p.42: tone has lexical, grammatical and syntactic function. No word on stress/accent (no 'klemtoon', 'accent', 'nadruk' anywhere in pp.31-42).

tone.quote: Cet échantillon du Cendó que nous présentons est du sous-groupe Ankutshu de la Zone de Kibombo (3). Il fut produit en novembre 1963 par la chanteuse Biibi Olowa Lokoso originaire de Bahina ... et enregistré sur magnétophone. Delo dyé wâná Lohahé (4) 1. Ndé kángi léé ! ... [note] 4. Le texte est traduit littéralement avec économie du tonème bas.
tone.locator: pp. 204-205 §3 'Echantillon du Cendo' and p. 211 note 4
tone.translation: This sample of the Cendo that we present is from the Ankutshu sub-group of the Kibombo Zone (3). It was performed in November 1963 by the singer Biibi Olowa Lokoso, a native of Bahina ... and recorded on tape. [chant title] (4) 1. What pain! ... [note] 4. The text is translated literally, with economy of the low toneme [i.e. low tone left unmarked].
